accepted.s: Western disturbances affecting north-western India are best described as:
o: Mediterranean temperate cyclones reaching India through Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan
Tropical cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal
Local convectional storms originating over the Thar Desert
Retreating monsoon winds originating over the Arabian Sea
accepted.x: Western disturbances are temperate cyclones originating in the Mediterranean region and reaching north-western India through Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Identify the origin and pathway of the weather system.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: Western disturbances are important for Indian agriculture mainly because they:
o: Produce rainfall on the Tamil Nadu coast during October
Bring heavy summer rain to the Deccan Plateau
Provide winter rainfall beneficial to rabi crops
Cause the onset of the south-west monsoon
accepted.x: Western disturbances bring about 10–15 cm of winter rain to north-western India, which is beneficial for rabi crops.
accepted.tq: Link a climatic phenomenon with its agricultural effect.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: Which of the following regions receives snowfall due to western disturbances?
o: Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
Tamil Nadu, Kerala and coastal Karnataka
accepted.x: Western disturbances cause snowfall in the hills of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
accepted.tq: Match the weather system with its characteristic area.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the retreating monsoon:
1. It is mainly associated with October and November.
2. It is generally accompanied by clear skies.
3. It may produce cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The retreating monsoon occurs mainly in October-November, brings clear skies and is associated with cyclones from the Bay of Bengal.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of characteristics through coded combinations.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: The term ‘October heat’ refers to:
o: A heat wave occurring exclusively in north-western India in April
Extreme heat caused by western disturbances
Hot and humid weather during the retreat of the monsoon
Cold and dry weather after the winter monsoon
accepted.x: October heat denotes the hot and humid conditions experienced in October as the south-west monsoon retreats.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a named climatic phenomenon and nearby seasonal conditions.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: The relative dryness of the Tamil Nadu coast during the south-west monsoon is mainly due to:
o: The permanent dominance of western disturbances
Its location on the leeward side and the winds blowing parallel to the coast
Its location north of the Tropic of Cancer
The absence of the Bay of Bengal
accepted.x: The Tamil Nadu coast lies in a rain-shadow position during the south-west monsoon, while the winds largely blow parallel to the coast.
accepted.tq: Apply the rain-shadow and wind-direction concepts to a regional example.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: North-west India during western disturbances — No winter precipitation
Tamil Nadu coast during south-west monsoon — Relatively dry
South India during retreating monsoon — Absence of cyclonic activity
Tamil Nadu coast during north-east monsoon — Relatively dry
accepted.x: The Tamil Nadu coast remains relatively dry during the south-west monsoon, but receives significant rain during the north-east monsoon.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched regional effect among reversed alternatives.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: Which of the following climate-type codes is correctly matched with its region?
o: Amw — West coast south of Goa
BWhw — Most of the peninsula south of the Tropic of Cancer
accepted.x: Amw denotes a monsoon climate with a short dry season and occurs on the west coast south of Goa.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure climate-code and region pair.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: The climate type BShw is associated with:
o: A cold humid climate with a short summer in Arunachal Pradesh
A semi-arid steppe climate in north-western Gujarat, western Rajasthan and parts of Punjab
A monsoon climate with dry summer on the Coromandel coast
A hot desert climate in extreme western Rajasthan
accepted.x: BShw represents a semi-arid steppe climate found in north-western Gujarat, western Rajasthan and parts of Punjab.
accepted.tq: Distinguish between similar Koppen climate codes by region and climate character.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Aw — Most of the peninsula south of the Tropic of Cancer
As — Coromandel coast and Tamil Nadu
Cwg — Ganga plain, eastern Rajasthan and northern Madhya Pradesh
accepted.x: ET denotes a polar or tundra climate found in the highlands of Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, not coastal Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong location attached to an otherwise familiar climate code.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: The climate type Dfc is characteristic of:
o: The west coast south of Goa
accepted.x: Dfc denotes a cold humid climate with a short summer and is associated with Arunachal Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive climate-region association.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: The north-east monsoon receives moisture mainly because retreating winds:
o: Pass over the Bay of Bengal
accepted.x: The retreating winds pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and bring rainfall to the Coromandel coast and adjoining areas.
accepted.tq: Trace the moisture source of a seasonal wind system.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: Which group of regions is specifically identified as receiving rainfall from the north-east monsoon?
o: Coromandel coast, Rayalaseema, Nellore and Prakasam
Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Kashmir
Gujarat, western Rajasthan, Punjab and Ladakh
Konkan, Malabar, Goa and coastal Karnataka
accepted.x: The north-east monsoon brings rainfall to the Coromandel coast, Rayalaseema, Nellore and Prakasam.
accepted.tq: Test the complete regional distribution rather than a single location.
accepted.sec: Climatic phenomena → effect in India

accepted.s: According to the India Meteorological Department classification, winter comprises:
accepted.x: Under the stated IMD classification, winter comprises January and February.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between competing seasonal month conventions.
accepted.sec: Seasons of India (IMD) - months, heat-wave period

accepted.s: The pre-monsoon or summer season, according to the IMD classification, extends from:
accepted.x: The IMD places the pre-monsoon or summer season in March-May.
accepted.tq: Test the exact beginning and ending months of a season.
accepted.sec: Seasons of India (IMD) - months, heat-wave period

accepted.s:
Arrange the following IMD seasons in chronological order beginning with winter:
A. South-west monsoon
B. Post-monsoon or north-east monsoon
C. Winter
D. Pre-monsoon or summer
accepted.x: The sequence is winter, pre-monsoon or summer, south-west monsoon and post-monsoon or north-east monsoon.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last seasons to narrow the chronological sequence.
accepted.sec: Seasons of India (IMD) - months, heat-wave period

accepted.s: The south-west monsoon season in the IMD classification covers:
accepted.x: The IMD south-west monsoon season extends from June to September.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise four-month seasonal block.
accepted.sec: Seasons of India (IMD) - months, heat-wave period

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding heat conditions in India is correct?
o: Heat waves generally peak in January and February.
North-western and central India are hottest mainly from April to June, with heat waves peaking in May-June.
The hottest period in north-western India is restricted to October-November.
Heat waves peak only during the south-west monsoon season.
accepted.x: North-western and central India experience their hottest conditions from April to June, and heat waves generally peak in May-June.
accepted.tq: Combine the season, region and peak-period clues.
accepted.sec: Seasons of India (IMD) - months, heat-wave period

accepted.s: Ganganagar is noted in the climatic record for having recorded approximately:
accepted.x: Ganganagar recorded approximately 50°C in 1935.
accepted.tq: Test a distinctive recorded temperature using closely spaced figures.
accepted.sec: Seasons of India (IMD) - months, heat-wave period

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the six traditional Indian seasons?
accepted.x: The six traditional seasons are Vasanta, Grishma, Varsha, Sharad, Hemanta and Shishira. Pravaha is not included in this list.
accepted.tq: Identify the outsider from a fixed traditional list.
accepted.sec: Seasons of India (IMD) - months, heat-wave period

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecasting System?
o: A polar vortex model introduced in 2021
A six-kilometre weather model introduced in 2025
A dynamic ocean-atmosphere-land model introduced in 2012
A statistical ensemble model introduced in 2007
accepted.x: The Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecasting System is a dynamic ocean-atmosphere-land model introduced in 2012.
accepted.tq: Separate models by name, year and modelling approach.

Consider the following pairs:
1. SEFS statistical ensemble — 2007
2. Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecasting System — 2012
3. Multi-Model Ensemble — 2021
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?

accepted.s: Ocean Mean Temperature is measured as the average temperature of the upper Indian Ocean up to the:
accepted.x: OMT is the average temperature of the upper Indian Ocean down to the 26°C isotherm.
accepted.tq: Recall the defining threshold of a specialised ocean indicator.

accepted.s: Which statement about Ocean Mean Temperature is correct?
o: It is measured in January-March and predicts monsoon rainfall better than SST.
It is measured in June-September and is less useful than SST for monsoon prediction.
It is measured only in October and predicts snowfall in the Himalayas.
It refers to the temperature of the entire Indian Ocean basin throughout the year.
accepted.x: OMT is measured during January-March and has been identified as a better predictor of monsoon rainfall than sea-surface temperature.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a specialised indicator from the related SST concept.

accepted.s: The Tropic of Cancer crosses how many Indian states?
accepted.x: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
accepted.tq: Test a fixed geographical count and its associated list.
accepted.sec: Controls of Indian climate - latitude, altitude, distance from sea, islands

accepted.s: Shimla is considerably cooler than Amritsar despite their similar latitude primarily because of:
o: The influence of the north-east monsoon
The absence of the Himalayas near Shimla
accepted.x: Altitude is the major factor making Shimla much cooler than Amritsar at a similar latitude.
accepted.tq: Apply the altitude control of climate to a paired-location example.
accepted.sec: Controls of Indian climate - latitude, altitude, distance from sea, islands

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the effect of distance from the sea on climate?
o: Coastal areas generally have continental climates, while interiors are maritime.
Coastal areas generally have equable maritime climates, while interiors have continental climates.
Interior areas always have lower temperatures than coastal areas.
Distance from the sea affects only rainfall and never temperature.
accepted.x: The sea moderates temperature in coastal areas, giving them equable maritime climates, whereas interiors generally have continental climates.
accepted.tq: Test a reversed coastal-versus-interior comparison.
accepted.sec: Controls of Indian climate - latitude, altitude, distance from sea, islands

accepted.s: Which of the following is a major climatic role of the Himalayas?
o: They cause only winter rainfall on the Tamil Nadu coast.
They prevent all rainfall in northern India.
They allow cold Central Asian winds to enter northern India freely.
They block cold Central Asian winds and force orographic rainfall.
accepted.x: The Himalayas block cold Central Asian winds and force air to rise, producing orographic rainfall. Without them, northern India would be much more arid.
accepted.tq: Connect a physical barrier with both its thermal and rainfall effects.
accepted.sec: Controls of Indian climate - latitude, altitude, distance from sea, islands

accepted.s: The climate of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is generally:
o: Semi-arid with a large annual temperature range
accepted.x: The maritime influence gives the Andaman and Nicobar Islands an equable and humid climate.
accepted.tq: Use the island-versus-interior climate contrast.
accepted.sec: Controls of Indian climate - latitude, altitude, distance from sea, islands

accepted.s: The Mascarene High is best described as:
o: A permanent high-pressure cell in the southern Indian Ocean near Madagascar
A seasonal low-pressure cell over north-western India
A high-pressure cell over the Tibetan Plateau
A temperate cyclone over the Mediterranean Sea
accepted.x: The Mascarene High is a permanent high-pressure cell in the southern Indian Ocean near Madagascar and helps drive cross-equatorial flow.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a pressure cell by location and pressure character.
accepted.sec: Mascarene High and Somali jet roles

accepted.s: The principal role of the Mascarene High in the south-west monsoon mechanism is to:
o: Block the north-east monsoon over Tamil Nadu
Drive cross-equatorial flow towards the Indian subcontinent
Generate western disturbances over the Mediterranean
Cause snowfall in the Himalayan region
accepted.x: The Mascarene High drives the cross-equatorial flow that contributes to the formation of the south-west monsoon.
accepted.tq: Link a pressure cell to the wind movement it generates.
accepted.sec: Mascarene High and Somali jet roles

accepted.s: The Somali jet intensifies the Indian monsoon in association with the:
accepted.x: The Somali jet, together with the Somalia Current, intensifies the monsoon winds.
accepted.tq: Match the atmospheric jet with its associated ocean current.
accepted.sec: Mascarene High and Somali jet roles
